note: Domain dispositions are explicit model semantic intent and remain distinct from input_fate bookkeeping. Runtime owns accountable_set and validates/reconciles every declared disposition against changes, state_patch, trace and the frozen snapshot; model declarations never bypass mutation/policy validation.
transformation_stage_constraints: runtime resolves accountable_set before model call
each accountable input appears exactly once in dispositions
no foreign disposition input_ref is allowed
declared disposition and actual changes/input_fate must reconcile without ambiguity
annotations and narrative are never disposition sources
commit_condition: accountable_set == declared_disposition_inputs AND foreign==0 AND duplicates==0 AND reconciliation_errors==0

reconciliation_rules.require: result_temp_ids is empty; no successor change lists the input in source_refs; the input keeps its status (an UPDATE of the same identity is allowed)
exactly one result_temp_id; it is a MERGE change whose source_refs include input_ref
reconciliation_rules.runtime_consequence: input -> MERGED when the code has MERGED, else SUPERSEDED

reconciliation_rules.require: at least two distinct result_temp_ids; each is a CREATE or MERGE change whose source_refs include input_ref
either a SUPERSEDE change targets input_ref (same-type replacement) or exactly one result_temp_id is a CREATE whose source_refs include input_ref (cross-type transformation such as PRP -> PD)

either an UPDATE targeting input_ref proposes state_patch.status=DEFERRED (codes that have DEFERRED) or exactly one result_temp_id is a successor with lineage to input_ref and state_patch.status=DEFERRED (codes without DEFERRED, e.g. PRP)
reconciliation_rules.runtime_consequence: input -> DEFERRED when the code has it, else SUPERSEDED

reconciliation_rules.require: result_temp_ids is empty; no successor change lists the input in source_refs; input_fate, when present, is REJECTED
reconciliation_rules.runtime_consequence: input -> REJECTED when the code has it, else SUPERSEDED

input_fate_cross_checks: input_fate is bookkeeping and may be omitted for an input; when present it must not contradict the disposition
REJECTED input_fate requires REJECT; REJECT forbids PRESERVED/TRANSFORMED input_fate
CONSUMED and NOT_USED never satisfy transformation coverage by themselves
no_hidden_transformation: every change whose source_refs include an accountable input must appear in that input's declared result_temp_ids
status_consequences_owner: StateCommitter (runtime); models never UPDATE a transformed input directly
